::: {#sol-why-shrink}

Applying @sol-relu-grad's reasoning to $g$, then @sol-linear-input-grad,
takes the [gradient](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/linear-regression.html#def-gradient) back one layer:

$$
\gradwrt{\vhidval_{\layeridx - 1}} \loss
= \tp{\matr{W}_{\layeridx}} \vbackerr_{\layeridx},
\qquad
\vbackerr_{\layeridx} = \gradwrt{\vz_{\layeridx}} \loss = g'(\vz_{\layeridx}) \odot \gradwrt{\vhidval_{\layeridx}} \loss,
$$

where $\odot$ multiplies entry by entry.
Each layer back multiplies the gradient by the slopes $g'(\vz_{\layeridx})$ and by $\tp{\matr{W}_{\layeridx}}$.
The [logistic function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/functions.html#def-logistic-function)'s slope is at most $\frac{1}{4}$ ([lds's bound on it](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/logistic-regression.html#thm-logistic-derivative-bound)),
and less where [unit](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-unit)s [saturate](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/backpropagation.html#def-saturation),
so unless the weights are large,
every layer shrinks the gradient by a factor less than 1,
and 10 layers multiply 10 such factors.
The [ReLU](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-relu)'s slope has no $\frac{1}{4}$ bound:
it is 1 at each [unit](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-unit) that is positive and 0 at each unit that is not.
In the ReLU network of @sol-deep-grad-norms,
the gradient going back still shrinks, both because the weights PyTorch starts with are small
and because the [unit](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-unit)s at 0 pass none of it back.

The weight gradient of layer $\layeridx$ is $\oprod{\vbackerr_{\layeridx}}{\vhidval_{\layeridx - 1}}$,
by @sol-linear-param-grad,
so its size depends on the layer's input $\vhidval_{\layeridx - 1}$ as well as on the gradient $\vbackerr_{\layeridx}$ at its output.
In the ReLU network the layer inputs grow toward the first layers,
which is why its weight [gradients](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/linear-regression.html#def-gradient) level off there while the gradients $\vbackerr_{\layeridx}$ keep shrinking.

:::
